# Code Review (Alibaba OpenCodeReview) · DSH plugin
Run a real review of the changes you just made with Alibaba OpenCodeReview, and get the result back
**as it is** — what was covered, which model answered, and why it failed.

- **No separate `ocr` install.** The binary ships with the plugin (Windows x64).
- **No API key to c
onfigure.** The review uses the model **your current conversation is already using**, forwarded thro

ugh a loopback-only bridge inside DSH (your key never enters the `ocr` child process).
- **Verifiabl
e conclusions.** Every review carries a coverage receipt: which hunks were included, which files wer
e excluded, and which parts have no conclusion.
## 30-second start
1. Install (skip if already installed):
[代码示例省略，未执行]
2. After you change code, click **“启动代码审核”** at the end of the turn. Its sub-line states the cost fi

rst: `N files changed this turn · ocr tier: ~3–10 min/file, billed by tokens`.
3. Read the result. O

ged this turn · ocr tier: ~3–10 min/file, billed by tokens`.
3. Read the result. Other entry points:
| Entry | When |

| Turn-tail button | The common one; appears only when this turn changed code |
| `/ocr-review` | Tr

igger from the composer |
| Say “review this” in chat | The model calls it on demand |
## What you see
**Before it runs** — the button's sub-line states the files changed, rough duration, and whether it
s** — the button's sub-line states the files changed, rough duration, and whether it will be billed.
**While it runs** — there is **no progress bar and no stop button** (ocr emits no incremental progre
ss); the tool-call row shows elapsed time. To stop, stop the turn (usage already incurred is not ref
e tool-call row shows elapsed time. To stop, stop the turn (usage already incurred is not refunded).
**When it finishes** — six fixed layers, top to bottom:
1. **Conclusion** — success/failure and the number of findings; a dry run (`preview`) says plainly t

hat it reached no conclusion.
2. **Coverage and cost** — `x/y hunks included`, excluded files, trunc

ated parts.
3. **Findings** — `file:line [severity]`, severity `[high]/[medium]/[low]/[ungraded]` (u

nknown severities stay ungraded, never downgraded to low).
4. **Next step** — how to recover after a

failure, or what else you can do after success.
5. **Provenance** — engine and route (model provide

r/model; whether it came from the current session or the DSH default).
6. **Appendix** — truncated o
utput, raw JSON, spill paths. This layer always exists.
**On failure** — a result code, a next step, and what it cost. E.g. `OCR_LLM_MISSING`: no usable mod
el route, **zero calls, zero cost**.
## Two engines
| Engine | Behaviour | Cost |
| `ocr` (default) | Runs the full OCR pipeline (deterministic engineering × LLM agent pipeline) | Bi

lled by tokens; 3–10 min/file; estimate given before it starts |
| `delegate` | No LLM call; produce
s a review spec in seconds (files + rules + diff) for the current model to audit | Free (uses the cu
rrent conversation's model) |
Both engines resolve the `ocr` executable first: `delegate` needs it to produce the spec, `ocr` need
s it to run the pipeline.
## Where the model comes from
The plugin opens a loopback-only bridge with a random token; `ocr`'s requests are forwarded to DSH's
ns a loopback-only bridge with a random token; `ocr`'s requests are forwarded to DSH's `llm.stream`:

1. A model selected in the settings page → use it;
2. Otherwise the model **the current conversation

. Otherwise the DSH default model;
4. Otherwise `OCR_LLM_MISSING` (nothing runs, nothing is billed).
Provider and model are always taken as **one route**; they are never mixed across providers.
## Settings
The settings page exposes four fields: **enabled / default engine / on-demand review**, plus **model
name / provider** under “Advanced”.
Model name, provider and the ocr path live in `config.json` (empty = automatic, see above). Changes
apply immediately; no restart needed.
## Common failures
| Code | Meaning | What to do |
| `OCR_NOT_FOUND` | `ocr` executable not found | It ships with the plugin; on other platforms provid

e one or set `ocrPath` |
| `OCR_LLM_MISSING` | No usable model route | Pick a model, or make sure DS

H has a default; zero calls, zero cost |
| `OCR_NOT_GIT_REPO` | Not a git repository | `git init`, o

r run elsewhere |
| `OCR_TIMEOUT` | Killed by the timeout | Narrow the scope (`scope=commit`) or rai

se `timeoutMinutes` |
| `OCR_ABORTED` | Cancelled | Re-run; usage already incurred is not refunded |

| `OCR_ALREADY_RUNNING` | A review is already running | Wait for it (one at a time) |
| `OCR_INVALI
D_ARGS` | Unsupported argument combination | Follow the suggested usage in the message |
## Troubleshooting
- `ocr_status` in one shot: where `ocr` came from (bundled/local), the effective model route, whethe

r event hooks are attached, and why the last review failed.
- No button? This turn changed no code.
The only exception is when the host cannot report the change list — then the button is always shown

(fail-open).
- Want faster feedback? Switch the engine to `delegate` in settings.
## Development
[代码示例省略，未执行]

- `npm run test:pack` asserts the published tarball contains only what it should.
- CI: `.github/wor
kflows/ci.yml`, Node 20 / 22 / 24 × ubuntu / windows.
## Known limitations

- The bundled binary covers Windows x64 (a macOS arm64 package exists but is unverified).
- Installi

ng downloads about 57 MB (the platform binary package); no build scripts run.
- Real-machine accepta

nce was done on Windows x64 only (macOS / Linux unverified).
- No progress bar (ocr emits no increme

ntal progress), so “how much longer” is a range.
- Reviews cover the **change set** (git diff); hist
orical issues elsewhere in the repo are out of scope.
